speaker: Doctor
text: That is a concerning presentation. Can you tell me how long this lesion has been present, and do you recall any specific event like an insect bite or minor injury when it started?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your history of Crohn's disease, uveitis, and diabetes, I am concerned about an atypical infection or malignancy triggered by that ant bite. Have you noticed any systemic symptoms like fever, night sweats, or weight loss, and does the lesion have any drainage or distinct borders?

REQUEST IMAGES: Full body skin photos focusing on the right leg lesion.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis. The combination of a painful, necrotic ulcer following an insect bite, alongside your history of Crohn's disease, anterior uveitis, and immunosuppression, strongly suggests a parasitic infection. Please see the images I requested; they will likely confirm the characteristic undermined borders of the lesion.
